faqs.a: Percent error compares a measurement against a known true value. Percent change compares two measured values over time, showing an increase or decrease.

howTo: Enter your measured (experimental) value in the first field.
Enter the accepted or theoretical value in the second field.
The calculator computes the percent error instantly as you type.

Repeat for multiple trials — the smallest percent error marks the most accurate measurement.
keyFacts: Percent error measures accuracy — how close a measurement is to the accepted true value.
The result is always expressed as a positive percentage, never negative.
Percent error can exceed 100% when the measured value is far from the true value.
Scientists and students use it in lab reports to judge the quality of an experiment.
It differs from percent change, which compares two measured values rather than a measurement against a true value.
A low percent error means high accuracy; 0% means the measurement matched the true value exactly.

percent-error-calculator.quickAnswer: Percent error tells you how accurate a measurement is compared to the true value. Subtract the true value from the measured value, divide by the true value, multiply by 100 and take the absolute value. A 0% error means a perfect match.
percent-error-calculator.tagline: See how close your experimental result is to the accepted true value.
percent-error-calculator.workedExample:
You measure the density of water as 0.98 g/cm³. The accepted value is 1.00 g/cm³.

Percent error = |0.98 - 1.00| / |1.00| x 100 = 0.02 / 1.00 x 100 = 2%.

Absolute error = |0.98 - 1.00| = 0.02 g/cm³.

The measurement sits 2% away from the true value — a solid result for a school lab experiment.
